transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-15 10:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Janelle Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Ruiz (Redwood SE), Elaine Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (AlphaHealth ML Eng), Marcus Lee (AlphaHealth CTO), Samir Patel (AlphaHealth SRE), Holly Gomez (Alpha Product)
Shared artifacts: drive.google.com/alpha-bench (benchmark sheet), /docs/redwood-security-snapshot.pdf

Summary: quick recap of last week's runs, results vs BaselineCloud, tuning applied (4-bit quant, KV cache), and agreement on longer 24h stability test.

00:00 - Janelle Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, we're going to walk through the latest numbers from the pilot — we ran the tuned config overnight and have side-by-side comparisons with your BaselineCloud numbers.
00:28 - Priya Nair: Great, thanks. I saw the sheet but haven't had time to dig into the new run details. Looking for p95/p99 and also end-to-end time from our frontend to model.
00:45 - Marcus Ruiz: Cool — quick note on infra: Redwood run used A100s (40GB) with fp16 runtime, 4-bit quant to save memory, and we enabled persistent KV cache for prefix repetitions. Batch target was 32 for high QPS windows; we also tested batch target 8 for low-latency windows.
01:12 - Marcus Lee: Can you remind me what the baseline was running on?
01:21 - Elaine Cho: BaselineCloud numbers we have were from their managed endpoint on T4s, default float16, batching at 16, and no KV cache. Also their autoscaler is conservative so we saw cold-starts during spikes.
01:38 - Holly Gomez: When you say "KV cache enabled" — is that keeping states between requests? Is there any data residency concern?
01:48 - Marcus Ruiz: It's an internal token-level cache of key/values, yes it's ephemeral and doesn't persist to disk. We treat it as in-memory for inference — no user PII stored, and we log hits/misses for debugging.
02:05 - Samir Patel: Ok, good. On network side, we care about egress and IPs — we'll follow up on allowlist but assumed fine for tests.
02:18 - Janelle Park: Walking the main metric table — p50, p95, p99 and sustained QPS. For the 512-seq synthetic trace: Redwood p50 42ms, p95 210ms, p99 420ms, sustained throughput 1,150 RPS. BaselineCloud p50 60ms, p95 380ms, p99 950ms, sustained throughput 760 RPS. These are median of three runs.
03:02 - Priya Nair: Those p99 numbers are pretty different. How consistent were they across runs? Any variance?
:03:12 - Marcus Ruiz: There was some variance on baseline because of cold starts and queuing due to smaller GPU memory on T4. Redwood runs were stable; stddev on p99 across runs was ~6-8%. For BaselineCloud it was ~22% because of autoscale delays.
03:40 - Priya Nair: Hmm ok. What about quality — did 4-bit quantization affect outputs? We do sensitive clinical summarization tasks.
03:51 - Elaine Cho: We ran a small eval set of 200 prompts comparing Redwood quant 4-bit vs baseline float16. BLEU/ROUGE-style automatic metrics showed <0.6% delta on average, and manual spot-checks found one case where specificity dropped slightly. We'll send the eval set and diffs.
04:18 - Marcus Lee: We need to see the actual examples. Can you annotate which ones are regressions and explain if they affect clinical correctness?
04:28 - Elaine Cho: Absolutely. We'll annotate and flag severity.

05:00 - Janelle Park: On batching tradeoffs — we showed a 12% cost reduction by increasing batching during steady state; but that increased p99 by ~30ms. With KV cache we got most of the cost win without the tail penalty.
05:24 - Priya Nair: Do you have a recommended policy for us? We want to keep tail low for UI but still save on cost at high QPS windows.
05:34 - Marcus Ruiz: We recommend dynamic batching: small batch target (8) for periods below 200 QPS, and larger batches with KV cache for above. Also route top 5% critical requests to a low-latency lane (dedicated nodes) — config we can expose in the console.
06:00 - Samir Patel: About the routing, what's the SLAs on those dedicated nodes? And can they be guaranteed during peaks?
06:10 - Elaine Cho: With Dedicated capacity you can reserve nodes; for pilot we simulated reserved pool of 2 nodes which covered peak in our tests. SLA for reserved capacity is available in enterprise contract.
06:24 - Holly Gomez: Back to numbers — can we see tail latency in a live dashboard? We need to show product stakeholders.
06:33 - Janelle Park: Yes we can expose per-route p50/p95/p99 and token-cost breakdown; we'll give you a dashboard share link and token-level cost tracking for the pilot.

07:05 - Priya Nair: One concern: our production request shapes have many short prompts with repeated prefixes (like patient meta). How much did KV cache help for such patterns?
07:20 - Marcus Ruiz: For repeat prefixes we saw 40-60% reduction in per-token compute time on cached frames, which translated to about 25% lower end-to-end latency on those prompt classes. The hit rate depends on prefix variety; your traces will help estimate real hit rates.
07:45 - Priya Nair: We'll provide traces — but we need to scrub PHI — we'll produce anonymized traces with consistent tokenization.
07:55 - Janelle Park: Perfect — that will help.

08:10 - Marcus Lee: On cost math: what's the ballpark per 1M tokens given your config vs baseline?
08:20 - Marcus Ruiz: In our test config with 4-bit quant and sustained batching, we estimate $68 per 1M tokens. BaselineCloud in their managed offering came to about $110 per 1M tokens on same workload — largely due to lower throughput and higher GPU cost per inference. We'll share the cost workbook with assumptions.
08:45 - Samir Patel: Are those numbers including network egress?
08:50 - Janelle Park: That's inference-only compute plus infra rental. Egress and storage are separate; we'll annotate the sheet with those items.

09:10 - Priya Nair: For the 24h run you mentioned — will that include spike patterns? We have heavy diurnal spikes.
09:18 - Marcus Ruiz: Yes we'll replay your 24h trace and also run a synthetic spike window to validate autoscaler and tail behavior. We'll capture metrics every second and dump traces for debugging.
09:29 - Holly Gomez: Who will own the run? Redwood or Alpha?
09:34 - Janelle Park: Redwood will run it if you provide the scrubbed traces and allowlist. We'll post logs and a summary sheet. Priya to provide traces; Marcus Ruiz to run and share results.

10:00 - Priya Nair: A couple of small items — BaselineCloud claims lower latency with shorter sequences; did you validate at 128 seq?
10:10 - Marcus Ruiz: We did. At 128 seq Redwood p95 ~85ms, p99 ~160ms, throughput ~2,200 RPS. Baseline p95 ~120ms, p99 ~310ms, throughput ~1,450 RPS. So Redwood still leads, but gap narrows at short sequences.
10:36 - Priya Nair: Good to know.

11:00 - Marcus Lee: Any surprises in memory or OOMs?
11:07 - Elaine Cho: No OOMs on A100; on T4 baseline we saw occasional queueing. With 4-bit quant we fit larger context windows and had more headroom for batching.
11:22 - Samir Patel: For production, we may want to try H100s — any difference?
11:28 - Marcus Ruiz: H100 will further reduce p99 by ~10-20% and improve throughput, but cost per-hour is higher; it's a tradeoff that the cost workbook will show.

12:05 - Holly Gomez: Security and compliance — we began a security review last week. Any missing docs?
12:12 - Janelle Park: We uploaded the security snapshot to the shared drive; we'll follow up with SOC2 scope and our privacy whitepaper. Priya/Samir to confirm any specific audit needs.

12:35 - Priya Nair: One operational question — how long to flip pilot to dedicated if we like the results? Is there a provisioning lead time?
12:43 - Elaine Cho: For Dedicated reserved capacity, we can provision within 48-72 hours once contract and sizing are confirmed. For Private (VPC) it's longer — typically 2-4 weeks depending on networking approvals.
12:58 - Marcus Lee: Ok that's reasonable.

13:20 - Janelle Park: To recap next steps: Redwood will run a 24h throughput test with Priya's traces, share annotated eval diffs on the quantization set, and update the cost workbook. AlphaHealth will provide scrubbed traces and confirm the allowlist. We'll tentatively reconvene next Tuesday for the AB plan.
13:45 - Priya Nair: Sounds good. A couple of quick clarifications on the action items you listed?
13:52 - Janelle Park: Yep we'll put the items in the sheet and follow up in email.

14:10 - Samir Patel: Minor note — please include raw latency distribution CSVs, we want to plug into our internal dashboards.
14:18 - Marcus Ruiz: Will do. We'll include per-second metrics, histograms, and raw request logs (anonymized).

14:35 - Holly Gomez: Thanks everyone.
14:40 - Meeting ends.

Notes: Transcription imperfect in a few places (speaker labels may be off, some acronyms expanded incorrectly e.g., S L A). Refer to shared Google Sheet for raw numeric tables and run ids.

Final short recap (sent in chat):
- Redwood shows p99 improvement ~2x vs BaselineCloud on 512-seq runs.
- Throughput sustained +50% in model config with 4-bit quant + KV cache.
- Quality delta small on eval set; Redwood to annotate regressions.
- Next: 24h replay with production traces, cost workbook update, AB plan for peak hours.
